chunks: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at al-Hajar (the Black Stone area), so he asked for water. Then a cup of brass/copper was brought to him.
Then a man said: 'Indeed, Abbad ibn Kathir dislikes drinking from brass vessels.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'
And he (peace be upon him) said to the man: 'Did you not ask him whether it was gold or silver?'

key_terms.الصُّفْر: Brass or copper metal; yellow-colored metal, distinct from gold (ذهب) and silver (فضة)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm/problem; standard jurisprudential phrase indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَكْرَهُ: Dislikes or considers reprehensible; in fiqh context implies treating something as makruh (reprehensible) or haram

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to drink from brass or copper cups in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was at the sacred Hajar (the area near the Black Stone in the Ka'ba) when he requested water and was given a cup made of brass/copper (al-Sufr). When a companion mentioned that Abbad ibn Kathir disapproved of drinking from such vessels, the Imam declared there was no harm in it. He then challenged the man with a pointed rhetorical question: why did he not ask Abbad whether the vessel was gold or silver? This shows that the actual prohibition is drinking from gold or silver vessels (which is explicitly forbidden in Islam), not from brass or copper. The Imam's response corrects a misapplied scruple by pointing to the actual legal basis of the prohibition.
